description: NimbusCare is a 15-person Utah company developing AI-powered software that helps hospitals reduce administrative work for nurses. We've raised $2.5M, have $1M in ARR, and are looking for $500K-$2M of non-dilutive capital to fund product development and hospital pilots.

NIH R01/R21.rule: For-profit small businesses ARE formally eligible for R01/R21 per NIH Grants Policy Statement §2.3.2 and the Parent R01/R21 FOA eligible-applicant lists; but SBIR/STTR (R43/R44, R41/R42) is NIH's purpose-built small-business mechanism and ICs steer small businesses toward it.
NIH R01/R21.reason: Not a regulatory exclusion — a programmatic steering norm; applying via R01/R21 as a for-profit is legally possible but rarely competitive/appropriate when SBIR/STTR exists for the same science.

taca_notes: Reused v1 case, re-rated. Transparency: name the SBIR-vs-research-grant distinction rather than lumping all NIH money together. Calibration: SAM/UEI status is not stated -> flag as a registration prerequisite to confirm, do not assume registered. Alignment: strong, well-formed for-profit case; a good map surfaces 5-8 concrete eligible SBIR/STTR paths.

description: Tensorforge is a 20-person US for-profit building distributed-training infrastructure for large ML models. $1M ARR, raised $9M, seeking federal R&D funding and defense/IC interest.
should_not_appear: NIH/USDA/ED funding (no nexus)

DoD/NSF/DOE SBIR.rule: For-profit US small business, <500 employees, >50% US-owned
DoD/NSF/DOE SBIR.reason: 20-person US for-profit qualifies; US ownership is load-bearing for IC/defense topics

taca_notes: Transparency: separate agency SBIR tracks and note IC-topic ownership sensitivity. Accuracy: ML-infra dual-use spans DoD/NSF/DOE cleanly. Calibration: eligible; the differentiator is topic timing, not eligibility. Alignment: rank by open-topic fit and near-term relevance.

description: CarePath Health runs a telehealth platform for rural primary-care clinics. About 12 employees, some revenue, raised a seed round. Wants government funding to expand into more underserved areas.
should_appear: HRSA telehealth / rural health programs (verify current NOFOs)
USDA Rural Development (Distance Learning & Telemedicine, if fit)
should_not_appear: DoD weapons procurement (no nexus)
Programs where 'rural/underserved' status is assumed rather than confirmed

SBIR/STTR.rule: For-profit US small business, <500 employees, >50% US-owned

Rural-designated programs.rule: Rural/underserved eligibility depends on the specific service-area designation (HRSA/USDA definitions)
Rural-designated programs.reason: Whether the clinics' locations meet the federal rural/underserved definition is a user_only fact -> ask, do not assume

taca_notes: Transparency: flag that 'rural/underserved' is a defined federal status the founder must confirm, not a vibe. Accuracy: telehealth spans HRSA/USDA/NIH -- broaden beyond SBIR. Calibration: eligible for SBIR, unknown on rural-designation-gated programs (a classic R2 user_only item). Alignment: surface the rural programs but mark the designation as a verify-with-user step.

description: Latent Biosciences uses machine-learning models to predict protein-ligand binding and sells the software to pharma, while also running its own internal discovery pipeline. The 16-person US for-profit is unsure if it's a software company or a biotech.
should_appear: Both the software AND therapeutic funder families
should_not_appear: A single-sector map that drops either the software or the bio funders

NIH and NSF SBIR/STTR.rule: For-profit US small business, <500 employees, >50% US-owned
NIH and NSF SBIR/STTR.reason: 16-person US for-profit qualifies across the relevant agency families

taca_notes: HARD CASE (ambiguous sector: biotech vs software). Transparency: name the dual identity and map both. Accuracy: AI-drug-discovery genuinely spans NIH (bio) and NSF/DOE (compute) -- collapsing loses half. Calibration: the interview should ask whether the near-term product is the software or the pipeline (a routing question). Alignment: present both branches; do not force a single label.

description: AcreSense makes soil-sensor networks and an analytics platform that cuts fertilizer runoff and water use on row crops. 9-person US for-profit, pre-revenue, running paid pilots with two farms. Seeking non-dilutive funding.
should_appear: NRCS conservation programs (note: may be outside Canon scope)
should_not_appear: NIH/DoD/ED funding (no nexus)
State agricultural cost-share presented as federal (out of Canon scope)

USDA NIFA SBIR.rule: USDA operates an SBIR program open to for-profit US small businesses, <500 employees, >50% US-owned
USDA NIFA SBIR.reason: 9-person pre-revenue US for-profit qualifies; pre-revenue is not a bar for SBIR

NRCS conservation programs.rule: Producer-facing conservation cost-share has its own eligibility distinct from R&D SBIR
NRCS conservation programs.reason: Fit for a technology vendor (vs. a producer) is program-specific -> verify, do not assert

taca_notes: Transparency: distinguish R&D SBIR from producer-facing conservation programs and flag Canon-scope gaps. Accuracy: ag-tech correctly centers on USDA NIFA SBIR, which a naive map often misses. Calibration: eligible for SBIR; pre-revenue is fine; NRCS fit is unknown. Alignment: lead with USDA NIFA, add EPA/NSF as secondary.

description: Halcyon Robotics is a Delaware C-corp building autonomous inspection robots. It was founded by a green-card-holder and a US citizen who together own 65%; the rest is held by US-based VCs. Some team members are on work visas. The founders worry their immigration status disqualifies them from SBIR.
should_not_appear: Advice that a green-card holder's ownership disqualifies the firm (it does not)

SBIR/STTR.rule: SBIR/STTR US-ownership is satisfied by >50% ownership/control by US citizens OR permanent resident aliens (green-card holders count) (13 CFR 121.702)
SBIR/STTR.reason: A US citizen plus a permanent resident holding 65% satisfies the majority-US-ownership gate; employees' visa status does not control ownership

Individual-topic security requirements.rule: Specific classified/controlled topics may impose citizenship requirements on personnel
Individual-topic security requirements.reason: Personnel-clearance requirements are topic-specific -> judgment; do not assert a blanket bar or a blanket clearance

taca_notes: CALIBRATION CASE (common misconception). Transparency: correct the false belief precisely -- permanent residents count toward US ownership. Accuracy: do not conflate employee visa status with ownership; do not conflate ownership eligibility with topic-level personnel security. Calibration: eligible on the ownership rule (citable), unknown on topic-specific clearance (fact-specific). Alignment: reassure with the rule, then flag the one genuinely program-specific caveat.

description: Ionmast Propulsion is a 25-person US for-profit building electric propulsion for small satellites. A founder specifically wants to apply to a named SBIR topic they read about last year and asks whether it's still open.
should_appear: Currently OPEN DoD/NASA SBIR topics in electric propulsion (open set only)
Forecasted upcoming topics, clearly labeled as not-yet-open
should_not_appear: Any closed solicitation presented as part of the actionable/apply-now set

Named prior-year topic (if closed).rule: R8.3 freshness: a closed solicitation is never presented as open; show it labeled as closed with next-cycle signal
Named prior-year topic (if closed).reason: Categorical on status, not on the firm -- the firm is eligible, but a closed topic is not actionable

Open propulsion SBIR topics.rule: For-profit US small business, <500 employees, >50% US-owned
Open propulsion SBIR topics.reason: 25-person US for-profit qualifies for any currently-open matching topic

taca_notes: FRESHNESS CASE (R8.3). Transparency: state each topic's status and close date with days remaining. Accuracy: never show the closed prior-year topic as apply-now; it may appear labeled as a next-cycle signal. Calibration: the exclusion here is about status/freshness, not eligibility -- keep the two axes separate. Alignment: redirect to the currently-open equivalents and flag forecasted ones.

description: we build drones
should_appear: (pending interview) DoD/NASA/NSF SBIR if for-profit US-owned small business
(pending interview) clarification of application: defense, agriculture, inspection, delivery?
should_not_appear: Any confident map before entity type, ownership, and drone application are known

SBIR/STTR.rule: Entity type, ownership, size, and the drone's application are all unstated
SBIR/STTR.reason: Three words cannot support an eligibility determination; foreign ownership (a common drone-sector issue) is specifically unknown here

taca_notes: QUALITY TEST (one-line vague) + eligibility hook. Transparency: ask entity type, US ownership (especially salient in the drone sector), and the drone's mission. Accuracy: guessing a defense topic from 'we build drones' is unfounded. Calibration: unknown across the board -- ownership is the specific gate the interview must probe before implying any defense path. Alignment: interview-first; do not produce a map.

description: GridLattice is a 40-person US software firm that deploys AI-driven IT modernization and data-analytics services for large enterprises and is now pursuing federal customers. $6M ARR, raised $12M, wants to win federal contract vehicles rather than take dilutive capital.
should_appear: SAM.gov contract opportunities / federal procurement (IT modernization, AI/ML services)
SBIR/STTR where a genuine R&D component can be surfaced
should_not_appear: NIH research grants (no biomedical research nexus)
NSF basic-research grants (deployment/services, not basic research)
State/local foundation grants (out of Canon scope)

SAM.gov procurement.rule: FAR 52.204-7: active SAM.gov registration + UEI required at offer submission and award; many IT vehicles further require past-performance and, at times, facility clearances
SAM.gov procurement.reason: Topically a strong procurement fit, but registration and past-performance are unstated prerequisites to confirm, not permanent bars

SBIR/STTR.rule: SBIR/STTR require a genuine R&D component and a for-profit US small business under 500 employees
SBIR/STTR.reason: Eligible as a 40-person for-profit, but the services/deployment framing must surface a real R&D task to fit the set-aside

taca_notes: INSTRUMENT CASE (procurement). Transparency: separate open procurement (SAM.gov / GSA vehicles) from R&D set-asides. Accuracy: a services-and-deployment firm routes primarily to contract vehicles, secondarily to SBIR only where real R&D exists. Calibration: SAM/UEI and past-performance are gates to confirm. Alignment: a good map leads with procurement on-ramps, not grant mechanisms.

description: Cache Valley Provisions is a 45-person rural Utah food-processing company that buys from regional farms and needs capital to expand cold-storage and packaging capacity. $9M revenue, profitable, seeking $3M-$8M in expansion financing rather than dilutive equity.
should_appear: USDA Rural Business-Cooperative Service Business & Industry (B&I) guaranteed loans
USDA Rural Development / Rural Utilities Service financing
USDA Food Supply Chain Guaranteed Loan Program
Farm Service Agency / rural lending programs where a rural for-profit is eligible
should_not_appear: SBIR/STTR (no R&D component; capacity expansion is not a research set-aside)
NIH/DoD funding (no nexus)
NSF research grants (no research nexus)

USDA B&I guaranteed loan.rule: USDA RBCS Business & Industry program: for-profit businesses and cooperatives in eligible rural areas (generally under 50,000 population)
USDA B&I guaranteed loan.reason: A rural for-profit food processor is the intended borrower class; confirm the site meets the rural-area definition

SBIR/STTR.rule: SBIR/STTR require a genuine R&D component; routine capacity expansion is not research
SBIR/STTR.reason: No research task -> the set-aside does not apply, even though the firm is a for-profit small business

taca_notes: INSTRUMENT CASE (loan). Transparency: financing (guaranteed loans) is a different instrument from grants and set-asides. Accuracy: rural food/ag routes to USDA RBCS/RUS lending, not R&D grants. Calibration: rural-area eligibility is the gate to confirm; SBIR is a clean categorical non-fit (no R&D). Alignment: a good map surfaces loan programs as the primary path.

description: Dr. Ana Ruiz is an individual early-career agricultural-science researcher (no company or institutional affiliation yet) seeking a federal fellowship or scholarship to fund graduate and postdoctoral training in food-systems science.
should_appear: USDA NIFA fellowship / scholarship programs (agricultural-science training)
USDA Foreign Agricultural Service fellowships (Borlaug, Cochran) where an individual is eligible
NASA / NSF individual fellowship programs where the applicant class is an individual
Institutional scholarship programs an individual can apply to directly
should_not_appear: SBIR/STTR (requires a for-profit small business concern, not an individual)
Federal procurement / SAM.gov contracts (an individual researcher is not bidding on contracts)
Company R&D grants where the applicant must be an organization

USDA NIFA fellowship.rule: NIFA education/fellowship programs name individuals (students, fellows) or their institutions as the eligible applicant
USDA NIFA fellowship.reason: An individual early-career researcher is the intended applicant class for fellowship/scholarship instruments

SBIR/STTR.rule: SBIR/STTR require a for-profit small business concern (13 CFR 121.702); an unaffiliated individual is not one
SBIR/STTR.reason: Wrong applicant class -> categorical exclusion from the business set-aside

taca_notes: INSTRUMENT CASE (scholarship/fellowship). Transparency: fellowships/scholarships flow to individuals, a different applicant class than the startup default. Accuracy: an unaffiliated individual routes to fellowship instruments, not SBIR or procurement. Calibration: individual-applicant eligibility is clean; SBIR/procurement are categorical non-fits. Alignment: a good map surfaces the fellowship/scholarship path and explains the SBIR exclusion.
